one_line: Turkic general of Muhammad of Ghor who became an independent sultan and early builder in Delhi and Lahore.

appearance.face: oval face, wheatish to light brown Central Asian-Indian complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, sharp dark eyes with thick brows, default expression calm and commanding with a hint of strategic focus
appearance.hair: black hair kept short and straight under a slightly tapered dark red quilted turban-wrap (early Sultanate style) with a simple narrow gold band at the base and no plume
appearance.costume: Knee-length, long-sleeved Turkic-style qabā (robe) of rich deep teal wool, front-opening and belted at the waist, with fine cream piping along the edges and cuffs, worn over a cream cotton under-tunic visible at the collar; loose straight trousers in warm sand-beige tucked into sturdy mid-calf brown leather riding boots; around the waist a broad dark brown leather belt with a simple brass buckle and a small dagger sheath; over the robe a sleeveless, slightly flared mail and lamellar composite cuirass in dull steel-grey with small rectangular iron plates laced over mail at the chest; a light, warm-grey wool chadar (shawl) draped discreetly over the shoulders and upper arms, pulled back when in motion; minimal jewellery—a plain gold signet ring on his right hand and a simple, short gold chain barely visible at the neck.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged Turkic saber (kilij-type) with a steel-grey blade, plain brass crossguard, dark brown leather-wrapped hilt, and a simple wooden scabbard lacquered in deep red, worn at his left hip and often held loosely in his right hand in a poised, martial stance.

ref_desc: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak is a mid-40s, sturdy Turkic commander with a short beard, dark red quilted turban, deep teal qabā over mail-and-lamellar armour, cream tunic, beige trousers, brown boots and belt, carrying a deep red-sheathed curved saber in a steel-grey and earth-toned palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Qutb-ud-Din Aibak: a mid-40s, athletic, commanding Turkic ruler with an oval, light brown face, sharp dark eyes, thick brows, and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache. His black hair is mostly hidden under a slightly tapered dark red quilted turban-wrap with a narrow gold band at the base. He wears a knee-length, long-sleeved deep teal wool qabā with cream piping at the edges and cuffs, belted at the waist over a cream cotton under-tunic visible at the collar. Over the robe is a sleeveless, flared mail-and-lamellar composite cuirass in dull steel-grey, with small rectangular plates over mail at the chest, and a warm-grey wool chadar draped across his shoulders. His loose sand-beige trousers are tucked into sturdy mid-calf brown leather riding boots. A broad dark brown leather belt with a brass buckle circles his waist, holding a small dagger sheath. His only jewellery is a plain gold ring on his right hand and a short gold chain at the neck. At his left hip hangs his signature slightly curved Turkic saber with a steel-grey blade, plain brass crossguard, dark brown leather-wrapped hilt, and deep red lacquered wooden scabbard, which he also holds in a poised, ready stance. Use a deep teal, cream, sand beige, dark red, steel grey, and brown colour palette, and show him from multiple angles so his face, turban, armour, robe, boots, and saber design are absolutely clear and consistent.
